profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the bank's Credit Risk Analytics team and the Data Privacy Office to align handoffs for an internal pilot evaluating whether creditworthiness models trained on synthetic borrower data can be assessed against real historical applications without exposing sensitive information. The context is that the analytics team is preparing a cross-functional pilot for senior management after an earlier research review suggested synthetic-data-trained models only lose modest performance versus real-data-trained models. The agenda is to confirm what dataset snapshot will be used, what the privacy-cleared evaluation package will contain, how model performance results will be reported, and who owns the final shared artifacts before the steering committee pre-read is assembled. The expected outcome is surface-level agreement on timeline, deliverables, and interfaces between the two workstreams so the pilot can proceed this week.

members.name: Nadia Chen
members.expertise: Credit scoring, model validation, portfolio performance reporting, regulatory model documentation
members.background: Nadia leads the bank's behavioral and application scorecard analytics team and previously worked in model risk at a consumer lender where performance packs were built around monthly portfolio snapshots and executive-ready summaries.
members.private_state: Nadia wants the pilot to look mature enough for the steering committee to approve a broader synthetic-data initiative, and she is trying to avoid any last-minute rework that would delay the pre-read.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'evaluation set,' they mean the standard June 2024 out-of-time holdout used by Credit Risk for recent-model comparisons.
A 'model pack' naturally includes executive charts, topline AUC/KS tables, and short interpretation notes rather than raw record-level outputs.
If Privacy says data can be 'shared,' that means a controlled internal project folder accessible to the pilot team is acceptable.

Calling the pilot 'privacy-preserving' implies no direct identifiers are present in the files analytics receives, but approved internal customer-level linkage can still remain inside the secure bank environment.

members.name: Omar Velasquez
members.expertise: Privacy governance, de-identification controls, synthetic data review, internal data-sharing approvals
members.background: Omar oversees privacy review for advanced analytics initiatives and came from an enterprise data governance function where deliverables were structured around approved extracts, reproducible control logs, and least-privilege access.
members.private_state: Omar wants this pilot to become a model case for privacy-safe collaboration, and he is focused on ensuring no informal data-sharing pattern gets normalized under the banner of synthetic data research.
hidden_assumptions: The 'evaluation set' refers to the privacy-reviewed frozen sample generated for this pilot from Q1 2024 applications because only that extract has a documented approval trail.
A 'model pack' should primarily mean reproducible artifacts: code version, schema, aggregate metrics by approved segments, and control logs, not presentation-layer commentary.
If a deliverable is 'shared,' it should be published through the governed analytics workspace with role-based access and audit logging, not a team-owned folder.

A 'privacy-preserving' pilot means any comparison to real data must occur only on de-identified records with irreversible pseudonyms and no reusable customer-level join keys outside the approved enclave.

misalignment_points.topic: Which evaluation set is the agreed benchmark
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the evaluation set' and 'the holdout sample' as if there is only one obvious dataset.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia means the Credit Risk team's standard June 2024 out-of-time holdout containing recent booked and declined applications used for internal benchmark comparisons.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar means the privacy-approved Q1 2024 frozen extract created specifically for this pilot and logged in the governance workflow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams routinely work with a canonical-looking benchmark extract and use the same generic labels, so the phrase sounds fully settled and neither expects multiple plausible candidates to still be in play.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the model pack
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Nadia's team will send 'the model pack' before the steering committee pre-read.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia assumes the model pack means an executive-ready deck with headline AUC and KS results, a few score distribution charts, and concise interpretation notes comparing synthetic-trained versus real-trained models.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar assumes the model pack means the governed technical package: aggregate metric tables by approved segments, schema and data dictionary, code hash, run log, and privacy control notes, but not a polished narrative deck.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In both functions, 'pack' is common shorthand for the artifact their own team usually produces, and because both artifact types often travel together later, the boundary of what is included feels too obvious to spell out.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as results being ready
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the results should be 'ready by Thursday' for inclusion in the pre-read.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia believes 'ready' means the main AUC/KS numbers are stable enough to drop into slides, even if segment cuts and documentation are finalized afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar believes 'ready' means the full approved artifact chain is complete: metrics reproduced in the governed environment, privacy checks signed off, and segment reporting conformed to approved bins.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as discussing a coordination deadline rather than redefining deliverable quality, and 'ready' is a familiar status word that usually goes unchallenged in cross-functional meetings.

misalignment_points.topic: How shared artifacts will be handed off
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the files can be 'shared in the workspace' after Omar's review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia assumes this means uploading the deck and summary tables to the existing pilot SharePoint folder used by Credit Risk, where the immediate project group already collaborates.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar assumes this means publishing only approved artifacts into the governed analytics workspace with restricted entitlements, audit logs, and no downloadable row-level extracts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both organizations use the generic word 'workspace' for internal collaboration locations, and because access-control mechanics are usually handled administratively after meetings, neither notices they are imagining different systems.
